questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Topic: peer feedback. Which sentence is the clearest perspective for an oral presentation? \

answer.text: A. Peer feedback is the topic of this presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names the topic but gives no point of view.

answer.text: B. Many students write papers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not state a presentation perspective.

answer.text: C. Feedback happens in school sometimes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and not focused enough.

answer.text: D. Peer feedback helps writers revise because classmates can notice unclear ideas the writer may miss.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a focused perspective that can guide the whole presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 Perspective: Reading aloud helps students catch confusing sentences. Which detail best supports the perspective? \

answer.text: A. Hearing a sentence can reveal missing words or awkward phrasing.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the perspective about reading aloud.

answer.text: B. Some classrooms have bookshelves.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is school-related but does not support the perspective.

answer.text: C. Students use pencils in many classes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is unrelated to reading aloud.

answer.text: D. Sentences can be written in notebooks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general and does not show why reading aloud helps.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.08 U06 L03 Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 Perspective: Students should use study groups before tests. Opposing view: Some students focus better alone. Which response is strongest? \

answer.text: A. Students who study alone are wrong.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unfair and does not respond thoughtfully.

answer.text: B. Study groups are always better in every situation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too absolute and ignores the opposing view.

answer.text: C. Some students focus well alone, but study groups can still help students hear explanations and test their understanding.

feedback.text: Correct. This fairly acknowledges the opposing view and returns to the main perspective.

answer.text: D. Tests are part of many classes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not address the opposing view.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L03 Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which phrase is most appropriate for an academic oral presentation? \

answer.text: A. a bunch of random stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This phrase is informal and unfocused.

answer.text: B. coherent support for a clear perspective

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase uses precise academic vocabulary connected to the lesson skill.

answer.text: C. things that are kind of helpful

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and weakens precision.

answer.text: D. school stuff we do

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not use academic vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.07 U06 L03 Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 A speaker repeats the phrase "small steps create real progress" throughout a presentation. What is the rhetorical purpose of this choice? \

answer.text: A. To remove all organization from the presentation

feedback.text: Incorrect. Repetition can support organization when used purposefully.

answer.text: B. To avoid having a perspective

feedback.text: Incorrect. The repeated phrase actually reinforces a perspective.

answer.text: C. To change the topic every few seconds

feedback.text: Incorrect. Repetition usually keeps focus rather than changing topics.

answer.text: D. To reinforce the central perspective for the audience

feedback.text: Correct. Repetition can help listeners remember the speaker's main point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 Which detail should be removed from a presentation about how tutoring helps students review difficult concepts? \

answer.text: A. Tutoring lets students ask questions about confusing steps.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports the perspective.

answer.text: B. Tutors can explain a concept in different words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports the perspective.

answer.text: C. The tutoring room has a poster with blue letters.

feedback.text: Correct. This detail is unrelated to how tutoring helps students review concepts.

answer.text: D. Students can practice problems with feedback during tutoring.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports the perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 Which plan has the strongest coherent focus? \

answer.text: A. Perspective, supporting reason, example, response to opposing view, final takeaway

feedback.text: Correct. This plan keeps the presentation focused.

answer.text: B. Topic, unrelated story, different topic, closing

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sequence lacks coherent focus.

answer.text: C. Funny opening, random fact, thank you

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not develop a clear perspective.

answer.text: D. Source title, unrelated image, second unrelated image, claim

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order is confusing and unfocused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.08 U06 L03 Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Perspective: Digital calendars help students manage deadlines. Opposing view: Some students prefer paper planners. Which response keeps focus? \

answer.text: A. Paper planners are useless and nobody should use them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unfair and too absolute.

answer.text: B. Calendars have dates and months.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not respond to the opposing view.

answer.text: C. Students should never choose what works for them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unreasonable and weakens the presentation.

answer.text: D. Some students prefer paper planners, but digital calendars can still help by sending reminders and making due dates easy to update.

feedback.text: Correct. This acknowledges the opposing view and returns to the main point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L03 Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which revision improves academic vocabulary in a spoken perspective? \

answer.text: A. "Stuff gets better" instead of "revision improves clarity"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This makes the wording less precise.

answer.text: B. "Revision improves clarity" instead of "stuff gets better"

feedback.text: Correct. This uses academic vocabulary that fits the presentation.

answer.text: C. "Things are okay" instead of "evidence supports the claim"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This loses academic meaning.

answer.text: D. "Whatever helps" instead of "effective strategy"

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 Which sentence would most likely weaken coherent focus? \

answer.text: A. This detail supports my perspective because it shows how students use feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sentence helps coherence.

answer.text: B. Another reason is that feedback can point out unclear evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports a feedback-focused presentation.

answer.text: C. Also, school lunches should include more fruit choices.

feedback.text: Correct. This shifts to an unrelated topic and weakens focus.

answer.text: D. A final example is a student revising a confusing claim after peer review.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This stays connected to the topic.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.07 U06 L03 Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 A speaker uses a question at the beginning: "What would happen if every student had a clear study plan?" What is the likely purpose? \

answer.text: A. To engage listeners and introduce the presentation's focus

feedback.text: Correct. An opening question can draw attention and point toward the topic.

answer.text: B. To avoid stating any main idea later

feedback.text: Incorrect. A question should lead into the main idea, not replace it.

answer.text: C. To confuse the audience on purpose

feedback.text: Incorrect. A purposeful question should support understanding.

answer.text: D. To prove that evidence is unnecessary

feedback.text: Incorrect. A question does not remove the need for support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Perspective: Students should use class feedback before final submission. Which supporting detail fits best? \

answer.text: A. Final submission buttons can be different colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not connected to using feedback and does not support the perspective about improving writing.

answer.text: B. Classrooms have different seating charts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail does not support the feedback perspective.

answer.text: C. Feedback can identify unclear explanations before the assignment is graded.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the perspective.

answer.text: D. Some students have backpacks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is unrelated to feedback and does not help prove why feedback improves writing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.08 U06 L03 Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which opposing view is written fairly? \

answer.text: A. Some students may prefer independent study because it allows them to focus without conversation.

feedback.text: Correct. This presents the opposing view respectfully and clearly.

answer.text: B. People who disagree do not understand anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unfair and dismissive.

answer.text: C. The other side is ridiculous.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This attacks the opposing view instead of stating it fairly.

answer.text: D. Nobody could ever have a different opinion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This denies the possibility of an opposing view.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 A speaker has four details. Which one best supports the perspective "Academic vocabulary helps listeners understand precise ideas"? \

answer.text: A. Some presentations happen in the morning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support vocabulary precision.

answer.text: B. Students sometimes use slides.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not focus on academic vocabulary.

answer.text: C. A classroom clock can be hard to see.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is unrelated to academic vocabulary and would distract from the presentation's focus.

answer.text: D. Words such as "credible" and "coherent" name specific communication qualities.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L03 Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 Which word best completes this academic sentence? "A focused presentation should maintain a _____ perspective." \

answer.text: A. random

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random ideas would weaken focus.

answer.text: B. coherent

feedback.text: Correct. "Coherent" means logically connected and fits the sentence.

answer.text: C. hidden

feedback.text: Incorrect. A perspective should be clear, not hidden.

answer.text: D. careless

feedback.text: Incorrect. Careless does not fit an academic presentation goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which presentation focus is too broad? \

answer.text: A. Peer review helps writers notice unclear explanations before final submission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is focused because it gives a specific point about peer review.

answer.text: B. School is important for many reasons.

feedback.text: Correct. This is too broad to guide a coherent oral presentation.

answer.text: C. Weekly planning helps students divide long assignments into smaller tasks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is focused and clear.

answer.text: D. Study groups help students compare quiz review strategies.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is specific enough to guide support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.07 U06 L03 Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 A speaker chooses examples about classmates' real study challenges. What rhetorical purpose does this choice serve? \

answer.text: A. It removes the need for organization.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Relevant examples still need organization.

answer.text: B. It changes the presentation into a poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The examples do not change the communication mode.

answer.text: C. It avoids the speaker's purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The examples likely support the speaker's purpose.

answer.text: D. It makes the presentation more relevant to the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. Audience-relevant examples can help the speaker achieve purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 Which sentence best returns to the main focus after an opposing view? \

answer.text: A. While some students prefer working alone, a brief study group can still help students test their understanding before a quiz.

feedback.text: Correct. This acknowledges the view and returns to the main perspective.

answer.text: B. That other view is wrong, so I will ignore it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is dismissive and does not strengthen focus.

answer.text: C. Anyway, lunch schedules are confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This shifts to an unrelated topic.

answer.text: D. Opposing views are not allowed in presentations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Opposing views can be addressed when relevant.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.08 U06 L03 Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 Which response weakens validity when addressing an opposing argument? \

answer.text: A. Fairly stating the opposing view before responding

feedback.text: Incorrect. This usually strengthens validity.

answer.text: B. Explaining why the main perspective still makes sense

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports a valid response.

answer.text: C. Misrepresenting the opposing view so it sounds weaker

feedback.text: Correct. Misrepresenting an opposing view weakens fairness and validity.

answer.text: D. Returning to the main claim after the response

feedback.text: Incorrect. This helps keep coherent focus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which detail supports the perspective "Oral rehearsal improves presentation clarity"? \

answer.text: A. Some rooms have chairs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This classroom detail does not connect to oral rehearsal or explain how rehearsal improves clarity.

answer.text: B. Presentation files can be saved on a computer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not about oral rehearsal.

answer.text: C. Students sometimes use pencils.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is unrelated to oral rehearsal and would not support the perspective about presentation clarity.

answer.text: D. Rehearsal helps speakers notice where wording sounds confusing.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.01 U06 L03 Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Which phrase is most precise for a presentation about opposing arguments? \

answer.text: A. opposing perspective

feedback.text: Correct. This phrase precisely names the different point of view.

answer.text: B. the other stuff

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: C. whatever they say

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and dismissive.

answer.text: D. some random idea

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and unfair.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.07 Which presentation plan stays focused on one perspective? \

answer.text: A. Perspective: feedback improves writing. Details: lunch menus, sports scores, notebook colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. These details do not support the perspective.

answer.text: B. Perspective: feedback improves writing. Details: feedback identifies unclear claims, feedback suggests stronger evidence, feedback helps revision.

feedback.text: Correct. Every detail supports the same perspective.

answer.text: C. Perspective: feedback improves writing. Details: school buses, cafeteria tables, hallway signs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. These details are unrelated.

answer.text: D. Perspective: feedback improves writing. Details: random facts, jokes, unrelated memories.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This plan lacks coherent support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.R.07 U06 L03 Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.R.08 A speaker chooses a respectful tone when addressing disagreement. How does that support purpose? \

answer.text: A. It makes evidence unnecessary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Tone does not replace evidence.

answer.text: B. It removes the speaker's perspective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A respectful tone can still support a clear perspective.

answer.text: C. It helps the audience consider the response instead of reacting to an insult.

feedback.text: Correct. Respectful tone supports persuasion and clarity.

answer.text: D. It prevents organization.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Tone and organization can work together.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.01 Which sentence is a coherent final takeaway? \

answer.text: A. That is all, and I also like music.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This adds an unrelated idea.

answer.text: B. Study groups are useful because they help students explain ideas, ask questions, and prepare with classmates.

feedback.text: Correct. This final takeaway restates the focused perspective.

answer.text: C. So, study groups, posters, and lunch all matter equally.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This mixes unrelated topics.

answer.text: D. The end is here now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This closes the presentation but does not reinforce the perspective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L03 Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 A student asks, "Does this detail help my audience understand my perspective?" What skill is the student using? \

answer.text: A. Checking whether support connects to the main idea

feedback.text: Correct. The student is testing whether details support the presentation's perspective.

answer.text: B. Avoiding coherent focus

feedback.text: Incorrect. This question actually helps maintain focus.

answer.text: C. Removing the audience from the presentation

feedback.text: Incorrect. The question includes audience awareness.

answer.text: D. Choosing random details

feedback.text: Incorrect. The student is doing the opposite by checking relevance.
